chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who intends to marry the woman, can he look at her? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. He is buying her with the highest of the prices.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to look at the woman he intends to marry before the wedding?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) permits a man to look at his prospective bride to ensure compatibility, framing the marriage contract as a significant transaction where due diligence is required. This ruling underscores the practical necessity of visual assessment in Islamic jurisprudence to prevent future discord, reflecting the Shia emphasis on mutual consent and awareness within the marital bond.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the man who intends to marry the woman, can he look at her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. But rather, he is buying her with the highest of the prices’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub af-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who wanted to marry a woman if he could look at her. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so because he wants to pay a high price/”
